title: Descent of the ordinary open tensor projection
statement: Fix the ringed sites, exact additive functors $F,G$, adjunction, site functor and section maps of [def-sf-open-tensor-cochain-data], and ordinary/cochain data $D$ for them. Fix closed derived tensor structures $A,A'$ and simultaneous K-flat models $T,T'$ in the conventions of [def-sf-open-tensor-representative-data]. Fix a representative-normalized restriction tensor isomorphism $\mu:A\otimes G\cong(G\times G)\otimes A'$ whose ordinary comparison is $D.\mathrm{pullTensor}$. Fix ambient and open one-flat-factor comparison families agreeing with $T,T'$ when both inputs are K-flat and natural on every pair of allowed chain maps. There is a natural derived projection isomorphism $\gamma:A(FM,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}F A'(M,GN)$ such that its inverse has adjunct $A'(\eta_M,1)\,;\,\mu^{-1}_{FM,N}$. For every arbitrary complex $C$ on the open site and every flat-term K-flat complex $P$ on the ambient site, the ambient comparison on $(FC,P)$, the inverse exact-$F$ factorization on $C$, and $\gamma_{Q C,Q P}$ compose to $Q(D.\mathrm{chain}_{C,P})$, followed by the inverse exact-$F$ factorization on $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes GP)$, $F$ of the open comparison on $(C,GP)$, and $F A'$ of the inverse exact-$G$ factorization on $P$. These are precisely the inverse-unit and representative equations of [def-sf-open-tensor-representative-data]. All other model data are inputs, not conclusions.

proof.text: Construct the inverse projection alpha pointwise by applying the inverse adjunction bijection to tensor(unit,identity) followed by inverse restriction. Naturality of the unit, the restriction isomorphism and the adjunction bijection gives naturality in both variables. The inverse-unit clause holds by the inverse law for the bijection.

On flat-term K-flat C and P, the resolving-pair mate square identifies the composite of the right representative comparison and alpha with the left representative comparison. Both comparisons are explicit composites of isomorphisms, so alpha is invertible on these representatives.

Every derived input is isomorphic to Q of a flat-term K-flat resolution: use essential surjectivity of Q and resolve a complex representative. Transport invertibility of alpha along the product of these isomorphisms using naturality. Pointwise invertibility makes alpha a natural isomorphism; set gamma to its inverse.

For arbitrary C and resolving P, resolve C alone. Chain naturality, exact-functor factorization naturality and one-flat tensor comparison naturality give commutative squares for the left and right representative comparisons. The naturality square of alpha and the already proved resolving-pair square show the desired square after precomposition with the localized resolution tensor map. The left comparison square shows that map is invertible, so cancel it. Compose with gamma to obtain the required hom representative equation.

theorem openTensorProjection_descent
    (D : OpenTensorCochainData.{c, v, r} J R J' R' F G adj H sectionPull)
    (restriction : A.tensor ⋙ G.mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (G.mapDerivedCategory.prod G.mapDerivedCategory) ⋙ A'.tensor)
    (restrictionModel : TensorComparisonModel.{c, v, r} J J' R R' G A A' T T' restriction)
    (hordinary : restrictionModel.ordinary = D.pullTensor)
    (ambientModel : RingedDerivedTensorComparison.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1} J R A)
    (ambientBoth : RingedDerivedTensorBothModel.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1} J R A T ambientModel)
    (ambientNaturality : RingedDerivedTensorNaturality.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1}
      J R A ambientModel)
    (openModel : RingedDerivedTensorComparison.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1} J' R' A')
    (openBoth : RingedDerivedTensorBothModel.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1} J' R' A' T' openModel)
    (openNaturality : RingedDerivedTensorNaturality.{c, v, r, (max c v r) + 1}
      J' R' A' openModel) :
    ∃ gamma : (F.mapDerivedCategory.prod (𝟭 _)) ⋙ A.tensor ≅
    (𝟭 _).prod G.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ A'.tensor ⋙ F.mapDerivedCategory,
      (∀ M N,
    (SheafOfModules.OpenTensorNormalization.exactDerivedAdjunction adj).homEquiv _ _
        (gamma.inv.app (M, N)) =
      A'.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom
          ((SheafOfModules.OpenTensorNormalization.exactDerivedAdjunction adj).unit.app M)
          (𝟙 (G.mapDerivedCategory.obj N))) ≫
        restriction.inv.app (F.mapDerivedCategory.obj M, N)) ∧
      (∀ (C : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R') ℤ)
    (P : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (J := J) (R := R) P)
    (flatP : flatTerms.{c, v, r} J R P),
    (ambientModel ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C) P (Or.inr hP)).hom ≫
        A.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app C) (𝟙 _)) ≫
        gamma.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj C, DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (D.chain C P).hom ≫
        F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app ((totalTensor.{c, v, r} J' R').obj
          (C, (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)) ≫
        F.mapDerivedCategory.map ((openModel C ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
          (Or.inr (restrictionModel.kflat P hP flatP))).hom) ≫
        F.mapDerivedCategory.map (A'.tensor.map
          (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 _) (G.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app P))))
